questions.stem: Which of the following best describes polling in I/O systems?

options.text: The CPU continuously checks the status of an I/O device.
The CPU waits for an interrupt signal from the device.
The device transfers data directly to memory without CPU intervention.
The operating system communicates with hardware through a device driver.

questions.explanation: Polling involves the CPU actively checking the status of an I/O device to determine if it needs attention. This can be inefficient as it consumes CPU cycles even when the device is not ready.

distractorRationale.b: This describes interrupt-driven I/O, not polling.
distractorRationale.d: This describes the role of a device driver, not polling.

questions.stem: What is the primary advantage of interrupt-driven I/O over polling?

options.text: It reduces the need for device drivers.
It allows the CPU to perform other tasks while waiting for I/O.
It eliminates the need for DMA.
It requires less hardware support.

questions.explanation: Interrupt-driven I/O allows the CPU to execute other instructions until the device is ready, improving overall system efficiency compared to polling, where the CPU is constantly checking the device status.

distractorRationale.a: Device drivers are still needed for both polling and interrupt-driven I/O.
distractorRationale.c: DMA is a separate mechanism that can be used with both polling and interrupts.
distractorRationale.d: Interrupt-driven I/O typically requires more hardware support than polling.

questions.stem: A CPU initiates a DMA transfer of 1024 bytes from a disk to memory. If the DMA controller can transfer data at a rate of 512 bytes per millisecond, how long will the transfer take? Provide your answer in milliseconds.
questions.explanation: The DMA controller transfers 512 bytes per millisecond. To transfer 1024 bytes, it will take 1024 / 512 = 2 milliseconds.

questions.stem: What role does a device driver play in an operating system?

options.text: It manages memory allocation for applications.
It facilitates communication between the OS and hardware devices.
It schedules CPU tasks for execution.
It provides network connectivity for applications.

questions.explanation: Device drivers are specialized software components that enable the operating system to communicate with hardware devices, translating OS commands into device-specific actions.

distractorRationale.a: Memory management is not the role of a device driver.
distractorRationale.c: Task scheduling is handled by the OS scheduler, not device drivers.
distractorRationale.d: Network connectivity is managed by network protocols and drivers, but not all device drivers provide this.

questions.stem: Discuss the impact of DMA on CPU performance during I/O operations. Include at least two benefits in your answer.
markingGuide: DMA reduces CPU involvement in data transfers, allowing it to execute other tasks.
DMA increases system throughput by enabling concurrent data transfers and CPU processing.
DMA minimizes CPU idle time during large data transfers.
questions.explanation: DMA allows data transfers to occur directly between I/O devices and memory, reducing the need for CPU intervention. This frees the CPU to perform other tasks, increasing overall system throughput and efficiency. By minimizing CPU idle time during large data transfers, DMA enhances system performance.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a disadvantage of polling compared to interrupt-driven I/O?

options.text: Polling requires more complex hardware support.
Polling can waste CPU cycles when the device is not ready.
Polling cannot be used with DMA.
Polling increases the need for device drivers.

questions.explanation: Polling involves the CPU actively checking the status of an I/O device, which can lead to wasted CPU cycles if the device is not ready. This inefficiency is a significant disadvantage compared to interrupt-driven I/O, where the CPU can perform other tasks until an interrupt occurs.

distractorRationale.a: Polling generally requires less hardware support than interrupts.
distractorRationale.c: Polling can be used with DMA, although it is less efficient.
distractorRationale.d: Device drivers are needed for both polling and interrupt-driven I/O.

questions.stem: If a CPU spends 10% of its time polling a device and the rest on processing tasks, how much time does it spend polling in a 5-second interval? Provide your answer in seconds.
questions.explanation: The CPU spends 10% of its time polling. In a 5-second interval, this amounts to 0.10 * 5 = 0.5 seconds spent polling.

questions.stem: Explain how interrupt-driven I/O can improve system responsiveness compared to polling.
markingGuide: Interrupt-driven I/O allows the CPU to execute other tasks while waiting for an I/O device.
When an interrupt occurs, the CPU can quickly respond to the I/O request, improving responsiveness.
Polling requires constant CPU attention, which can delay response to other tasks.
questions.explanation: Interrupt-driven I/O improves system responsiveness by allowing the CPU to perform other tasks while waiting for an I/O device to be ready. When the device signals an interrupt, the CPU can quickly handle the I/O request, reducing delays. In contrast, polling requires the CPU to constantly check the device status, which can delay responses to other tasks.

questions.stem: Which mechanism allows data transfer between an I/O device and memory without continuous CPU intervention?

options.text: Polling
Interrupt-driven I/O
Direct Memory Access (DMA)
Device drivers

questions.explanation: Direct Memory Access (DMA) allows data to be transferred directly between an I/O device and memory, reducing the need for continuous CPU intervention. This improves system efficiency by freeing the CPU to perform other tasks.

distractorRationale.b: Interrupt-driven I/O involves CPU intervention to handle interrupts.
distractorRationale.d: Device drivers facilitate communication but do not handle data transfers directly.
